human.problem: In this oracle, the first-person voice ('My heart cries out' 15:5, 'I will bring more' 15:9, 'I weep' 16:9, 'I have put an end' 16:10, 'my heart laments' 16:11) could be the prophet or the LORD. Isaiah 16:13 calls the whole thing 'the message that the LORD spoke.' The walkthrough names the LORD for some of these lines and 'the speaker' for others. papa-dorin.md says to name who it is before quoting an 'I', but the Scripture rules say to leave open what the text leaves open.
human.question: When a prophetic passage speaks as 'I' and the text doesn't say whether it's the prophet or the LORD, should Papa Dorin name a speaker (and if so, which one), or always say 'the speaker' and leave it open?
